evidence: (a) Ownership is present under different terms: SOFTWARE-FACTORY-VISION.md:43 assigns the foreman to 'account for outcomes'; :71 assigns task recipes ownership and completion/handoff conditions, with progress owned by the work system; :97 requires remaining work to be recorded for successors. :75-77 describes load and recovery of live commitments and recurring jobs. (b) The contract makes dormancy normal (:39, :93) and says automation/delegation grows by explicit project choice (:25, :153); the promise at :11 does not specify continuous liveness surveillance. (c) CURRENT-DESIGN.md:9,58 and DESIGN-NOTES.md:183-187 explicitly keep project tasks out of graph; graph reconciliation and summarizer activation (:15-17, :32-34) are limited to their stated operations, so a general project-worker wake contract cannot be demanded of graph. (d) A factory-level stalled-work practice could be useful later, but absent a promised unattended-supervision SLA or specified first-project workflow, its omission does not contradict the draft's continuing ownership and recoverable-context outcomes. External comparison verified by fetching the current primary source https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/blob/main/docs/architecture.md : 'A zero-token bash watcher ... wakes the first mate only when something is actionable' (Event-driven supervision, lines 196-200). This establishes Firstmate's alternative mechanism, not a parity requirement. Narrowing: the claim that no owner is defined is false; detailed stalled-work detection remains an open future factory/instance design choice.
